Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: Unit 1. Nice to meet you!
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: World of people
- Materials: World map, country cards, survey sheet, COSYmanuals 'question words' and 'to be' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• discuss global nationalities and cultural backgrounds
• use Wh- question intonation

Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

foreign — from another country. Example: She speaks two foreign languages.
language — a system of words people speak. Example: English is a world language.
speak — to say words. Example: She can speak three languages.
passport — a document for international travel. Example: You need a passport to travel.
world — the earth and all people. Example: She is famous around the world.
country — a nation with its own government. Example: Which country are you from?
nationality — the country you belong to. Example: What is your nationality?
travel — to go to another place. Example: I want to travel to Italy.
learn — to get new knowledge or skills. Example: I learn English every day.
culture — the way of life of a group. Example: I like learning about other cultures.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Where are you from? (asking about origin)
• What language do you speak? (asking about language)
• I speak... (stating language)
• I have a passport. (talking about travel documents)
• People from many countries... (describing diversity)
• I want to learn about... (expressing interest)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'from another country'?
Which word means 'a system of words people speak'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Wh- question intonation and the /w/ sound in 'world'

world /wɜːld/ — one syllable
foreign /ˈfɒrən/ — stress the first syllable
passport /ˈpɑːspɔːt/ — stress the first syllable
culture /ˈkʌltʃə/ — stress the first syllable

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use question words to ask for different kinds of information.

Form:
Question words: Who (person), what (thing), where (place), when (time), why (reason), how (manner), how many (number). Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb.

Examples:
• Where are you from?
• Who is your teacher?
• How many brothers have you got?
• Why are you late?
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
___ are you from?
___ is your best friend?
___ many sisters have you got?
___ is your birthday?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• ___ is your teacher? (Who / Where / When)
• ___ do you live? (Where / Who / Why)
• ___ many people are in your family? (How / What / Who)
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What is your name?
• Where are you from?
• How many people are in your family?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three questions about your partner's family.
• Write three questions about your partner's home.
Reading: World of people

We live in a big world of people. Many foreign students speak English and carry a passport when they travel. People from many countries learn English for work, study, and travel. I want to learn about other cultures. Where are you from? What language do you speak? How many countries have you visited?
Why do many students learn English?
What do travellers carry?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Where are you from?
B: I'm from Brazil. And you?
A: I'm from Japan. What language do you speak?
B: I speak Portuguese and English.
A: How many countries have you visited?
B: I have visited five countries.
Where is the first speaker from?
How many countries has the speaker visited?
Speaking task: Survey three classmates about their country, language, and travel. Report two answers.

• Where are you from?
• What language do you speak?
• How many countries have you visited?
• Why do people learn English?
• Which culture do you want to learn about?
Role-play: You are at an international food festival. Meet people from three countries and ask about their culture.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about people from different countries.
Model: He/She is from ... He/She speaks ... People ...
